title: Business Development Executive
description:
Senior Business Development Executive

Salary: 30,000 - 40,000 depending on industry experience
+ Uncapped Commission
Location: Warwickshire - full time office based

We are looking for a driven and ambitious Senior Business Development Executive to join a growing organisation within the energy sector.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced sales professional to win new business, develop customer relationships and grow a portfolio of mid-market and SME clients.

The Role
- Generate new business through proactive outbound sales, cold calling and self-generated leads.
- Manage and develop a portfolio of SME and mid-market customers.
- Build relationships with key decision-makers and negotiate energy supply contracts.
- Manage your own sales pipeline, forecasts and sales targets.
- Engage with customers via telephone, email and occasional face-to-face meetings.
- Build relationships with energy supplier partners and deliver excellent customer service.
- Attend networking events and field-based meetings where required.

About You
- Minimum 2 years' sales experience, within B2 B.
- Experience in the Energy industry is desirable, similar/transferrable industry experience will be considered.
- Proven track record of achieving or exceeding sales targets.
- Excellent communication, relationship-building and negotiation skills.
- Confident engaging with business decision-makers.
- Strong pipeline management and organisational skills.
- Self-motivated, resilient and results-driven.

What's on Offer?
- Uncapped commission.
- Early finish on Fridays.
- Friendly, supportive working environment.
- Regular company events.

If you're a target-driven sales professional looking for your next opportunity with excellent earning potential, send your CV to Lily at Viqu Energy today!

title: Commercial Property Paralegal
description:
Commercial Property Paralegal Warwickshire Salary DOE

A quality role, a supportive team and the opportunity to take real ownership of your work.

I'm working with a leading law firm looking to bring an experienced Commercial Property Paralegal into its team in Warwickshire.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys commercial property work and wants to be part of a firm that gets the balance right: high-quality work, genuine autonomy and a working environment where people feel supported and valued.

You'll have the opportunity to play an important role in the team, take ownership of your workload and work on a varied range of commercial property matters, with the support of experienced colleagues around you.

Importantly, this is a role where the emphasis is on doing good work in the right environment. If you're looking to move away from an overly pressured or volume-driven set-up and into a team that values quality, collaboration and a manageable workload, this could be well worth exploring.

What makes this opportunity stand out?
- Quality of work: Exposure to a varied caseload of commercial property matters, giving you the opportunity to build on your existing experience.
- Autonomy and ownership: The chance to take responsibility for your work, play an active role in transactions and make a genuine contribution to the team.
- A supportive culture: Work alongside approachable, experienced colleagues who value teamwork and provide support when you need it.
- A manageable workload: A more balanced approach, allowing you to focus on delivering quality work without the expectation of simply processing volume.
- Long-term development: An opportunity to continue building your commercial property expertise within a leading firm that offers a positive environment to grow.

Who would suit this role?

I'm keen to speak with experienced Commercial Property Paralegals who have a solid grounding in commercial property transactions, take pride in their work and are looking for a role where they can develop their expertise while enjoying the environment they work in.

You might already be happy in your current position but feel ready for a change of environment, or perhaps you're looking for greater responsibility and a team that offers the right level of support.

Either way, if quality of work, culture and work-life balance are important to you, this is an opportunity worth a conversation.

Location: Warwickshire

Salary: Dependent on experience

If you'd like to hear more, get in touch for a confidential discussion. I'd be happy to talk you through the opportunity and give you a better feel for the team and what the role could offer.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Your new company
Hays are delighted to be supporting a high-growth SME business based in Warwickshire just outside Stratford-upon-Avon.

You'll take ownership of an allocated sales ledger, proactively managing outstanding debt, improving cash collection and building strong relationships with a varied customer base.

This is a great opportunity to join a growing business where you can make a genuine impact on cashflow and become a key part of the finance team.Salary: 28,000- 30,000 depending on experience + company benefits.

description:
Customer Complaints Handler

Location: Warwick, Warwickshire option to work from home on Mondays after training
Salary: £30,308 + Excellent Benefits
Job Type: Full-time or part-time considered for exceptional candidate

Are you an experienced Customer Complaints Handler looking for your next career move? Do you have a strong background in investigating complex complaints and delivering fair customer outcomes?

We re recruiting for an experienced Customer Complaints Handler to join a supportive team in Warwick. You ll take ownership of complex and escalated complaints from initial investigation through to final resolution, ensuring each case is handled professionally, fairly and in line with FCA regulations.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong investigative skills, sound judgement and experience writing high-quality final response letters.

- BUPA private medical cover, Medicash, Critical illness cover and death-in-service benefits
- Employee Assistance Programme, Long Service Awards, Employee Appreciation Day

- Investigate and resolve complex and escalated customer complaints.
- Manage cases from initial investigation through to final outcome.
- Prepare clear, accurate and well-reasoned final response letters in line with FCA requirements.

What We re Looking For in a Customer Complaints Handler
- Previous experience handling customer complaints, ideally within a regulated or financial services environment.

- Good knowledge of FCA complaint-handling requirements.

- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage cases independently.

Apply Today

If you re an experienced complaints professional who can confidently investigate complex cases, write effective final responses and deliver fair customer outcomes, we d like to hear from you.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant / Bookkeeper
Location: Warwickshire
Salary: £27,000 - £30,000
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:30pm
Contract: Permanent, Full Time, Onsite

We're working with a well-established and growing SME that provides specialist services to a national customer base. Due to continued growth, they are looking to appoint an Accounts Assistant to join their friendly and supportive team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly and no two days look quite the same. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting both the finance function and wider business operations.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintaining accurate financial records and supporting daily transactional finance activities
- Assisting with the processing and reconciliation of company accounts
- Raising and issuing client invoices
- Monitoring and following up on outstanding payments
- Handling customer and supplier enquiries via telephone and email
- Processing incoming supplier invoices and expenses
- Supporting month-end and reporting activities
- Maintaining financial data and ensuring records remain accurate and up to date
- Assisting with internal administration and operational processes
- Providing general support to the wider team as required

The ideal candidate will be organised, proactive and comfortable managing a varied workload within a busy office environment.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience in a finance assistant, finance officer, accounts assistant or bookkeeper role
- Experience using accounting software, ideally Sage 50
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel
- Excellent communication and customer service skills
- A high degree of accuracy and attention to detail
- The ability to prioritise tasks and work independently
- A positive attitude and willingness to support colleagues
- A flexible approach and eagerness to learn
- Due to the rural location of the office and limited public transport links, applicants must hold a full UK driving licence and have access to their own vehicle for commuting purposes.
- Full right to work in the UK is essential.

What's on Offer?
- Generous annual leave entitlement with additional service-related increases
- Health and wellbeing support initiatives
- Professional development and ongoing training opportunities
- Regular team-building and social events
- On-site parking
- Employee fitness and wellbeing benefits
- Supportive and collaborative working culture with genuine opportunities for long-term progression

Joining this business offers the opportunity to become part of a small & growing organisation that values its people, invests in development, and provides a varied role where you can make a real impact from day one.

If you're looking for a stable position within a positive team environment and have a background in finance administration, we'd love to hear from you.

Application Disclaimer: Due to the high volume of applications we receive, we are unfortunately unable to provide individual feedback to all applicants. If you have not heard from us within three weeks of submitting your application, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion.

Thank you for taking the time to apply.

title: HR Assistant
company: HR Dept - South Warwickshire - Agency - Permanent
description:
This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive and friendly HR consultancy team based in Warwick, providing high-quality administrative support across a varied client base. The role would suit a highly organised, detail-focused administrator who enjoys working in a busy, people-focused environment and is keen to build a long-term career in HR. Previous HR experience would be beneficial but is not essential, as full support, training and exposure to a wide range of HR matters will be provided.

Why Join Us

You will be joining a collaborative team where no two days are the same, gaining hands-on experience across employee relations, recruitment administration, HR documentation, client systems and general HR support. The role offers the chance to learn from experienced HR professionals, attend meetings alongside HR Advisors and develop practical HR knowledge while contributing to meaningful work for clients.

Training and Progression: Training and support will be provided, with the opportunity to develop HR knowledge and progress within the role.

Job Purpose

The role of the job is to provide excellent administrative support to the HR Advice team, helping to deliver a responsive, accurate and professional service to clients while developing practical HR knowledge and experience.

Main Duties
- Drafting HR letters as directed by the team including, disciplinary invites, grievance invites, outcome letters, letters of concern, resignation letters, flexible working letters etc.
- Drafting contracts and offer letters.
- Providing an effective service for our clients.
- Attending meetings with a HR Advisor to develop knowledge and experience.
- Answering incoming calls, taking details and supporting the clients where able to or providing accurate messages to the team in a timely manner.
- Support recruitment campaigns for clients, including drafting job adverts, shortlisting candidates and arranging interviews
- Uploading advice to the CRM system
- Liaising with third party providers e.g. occupational health, DBS
- Supporting the team with administration in relation to clients HR systems
- Note taking during meetings and note typing of meetings and recordings
- Supporting the team with creation and updating of handbooks, policies and contacts for clients

Qualifications and Experience Required for This Role

We are particularly interested in hearing from strong administrators who are highly organised, accurate and keen to develop a career within HR. HR experience would be advantageous, but it is not essential for the right person.
- Outstanding business organisational skills
- HR experience would be advantageous but is not essential.
- Strong administrator
- Self-motivated, able to take initiative and use sound judgment in day-to-day decision making
- Customer-focused with a 'can do' attitude
- Ability to work to tight and often conflicting deadlines in a fast paced working environment
- Ability to work accurately, with meticulous attention to detail
- Able to work with complete discretion and confidentiality at all times
- Expertise of MS Office (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook)

title: PMO Coordinator & Document Controller
description:
Pontoon is an employment consultancy. We put expertise, energy, and enthusiasm into improving everyone's chance of being part of the workplace. We respect and appreciate people of all ethnicities, generations, religious beliefs, sexual orientations, gender identities, and more. We do this by showcasing their talents, skills, and unique experience in an inclusive environment that helps them thrive.

Job Title: PMO Coordinator & Document Controller

Location: Warwick / Hybrid

Contract Type: 6 months contract with scope to extend

Role Overview

This role sits within a major infrastructure transformation programme and is responsible for the control, governance, and secure handling of sensitive, confidential, and encrypted project documentation and information.

Working within a structured PMO and project controls environment, the Document Controller ensures that all programme information is correctly classified, securely managed, version-controlled, and fully auditable across the project lifecycle.

This role is critical to maintaining information integrity, compliance, and governance standards across all project documentation, including regulated and protectively marked materials.

Key Responsibilities

Secure Document Control & Governance
- Manage the full lifecycle of controlled and sensitive programme documentation
- Ensure all documents are correctly classified, versioned, and securely stored
- Maintain strict adherence to document control procedures for protectively marked / confidential information
- Control document distribution, access permissions, and encryption compliance
- Ensure traceability of all document changes and approvals

Information Management & PMO Support
- Maintain structured document repositories and controlled data environments (e.g. SharePoint / CDE platforms)
- Support PMO governance processes through accurate documentation control
- Maintain registers, logs, and information tracking systems (RAID, change logs, action trackers)
- Support audit readiness by ensuring all records are complete, consistent, and retrievable

Data Integrity & Quality Assurance
- Conduct routine quality checks on documentation and data records
- Identify and resolve inconsistencies in document versions, metadata, and classification
- Escalate data integrity or compliance risks to PMO leadership
- Support continuous improvement of document control processes

Secure Digital & BIM-Related Information Handling
- Coordinate secure submission, storage, and retrieval of digital project information
- Maintain controlled records relating to model/data submissions where applicable
- Track document/model status through review and approval workflows
- Ensure secure handling of digital outputs from design and engineering teams

(This is coordination and control-focused - not technical BIM production)

Stakeholder & Supplier Information Control
- Act as the primary point of contact for document control queries across project teams and suppliers
- Manage secure access requests and permissions for controlled systems
- Support onboarding/offboarding relating to information access rights
- Ensure external parties comply with programme information control standards

Skills & Experience

Essential
- Proven experience as a Document Controller in a project, programme, or infrastructure environment
- Strong understanding of secure document handling, confidentiality, and access control
- Experience working with controlled or sensitive information (e.g. protectively marked data)
- Strong knowledge of document management systems (SharePoint, Aconex, A-Site, or similar CDE platforms)
- High attention to detail and strong organisational discipline
- Experience maintaining version control, metadata standards, and audit trails

Desirable
- Experience in regulated sectors (utilities, defence, rail, energy, construction)
- Familiarity with ISO 19650 information management principles
- Exposure to BIM/digital engineering information workflows (administrative support only)
- Experience supporting audits or compliance reviews
- Experience handling encrypted or security-controlled documentation environments

Key Performance Indicators
- Accuracy and compliance of document classification and version control
- Timeliness of document processing and distribution
- Audit readiness of document repositories
- Reduction in document errors, duplication, or misclassification
- Compliance with secure information handling procedures

description: An exciting opportunity has arisen to join our secretarial, clerical & administrative Haematology and Oncology team at Warwick Hospital. The structure provides ideal opportunities for career progression within the Haematology / Oncology team. If you possess excellent communication and organisational skills, work well in a team and can meet deadlines successfully then this position could be for you. The role will give the successful candidate experience of administration duties within a well established team and builds professional relationships with different disciplines within an NHS organisation. Please be aware, if we receive a large number of applications, we may close this vacancy earlier. To work as part of an administration team providing high quality day to day administration and clerical support to the Haematology and Oncology Services. To use own initiative, be responsible for own time management and prioritisation of workload. The role requires excellent communication, organisational and IT skills. Knowledge skills and experience required: To be responsible for providing administrative and clerical support using advanced skills in office procedures, systems and Information Technology. Using effective communication skills in all interactions with patients, clinicians, managers and colleagues within the Haematology and Oncology Service and other relevant departments. To be the first point of contact in dealing with enquiries both in person and on the telephone, in a professional polite and helpful manner and ensure urgent matters are brought to the attention of the person responsible, so that responses are dealt with quickly and within set guidelines. Will be responsible for processing correspondence/telephone enquiries and dealing with these routine requests using, own initiative. To arrange meetings, notify attendees initiate and prepare agenda. To take, transcribe minutes and meeting actions as required to cascade to internal/external delegates. To undertake general office duties as necessary, including filing, scanning, photocopying, taking notes of meetings, management and disposal of confidential information, as part of an effective administration service. To be responsible for sorting all incoming and outgoing post. To work as an effective team member, networking contributing to meetings to problem solve, improve working processes and practice. To monitor the supplies of office stationery and equipment within their locality. To provide administration cover in the event of absence or to meet additional demands or other circumstances where a service need is created. Participating in the maintenance of effective office systems, identifying improvements to improve individual, team and service performance. With direction and instruction to collect information required for statistical analysis and to collate information for forwarding to the relevant team. To use Trust EPR to record/process patient information as required by the Haematology and Oncology management team. Organising own work load and undertake other duties that may be required from time to time that are designated by the Haematology and Oncology management team. To exercise good personal time management, punctuality and consistent reliable attendance. To be responsible for maintaining designated work areas in a professional manner in accordance with Trust policies and procedures. Measurable Result areas: To process sensitive, complex information in line with Trust policy/procedure and to liaise with the appropriate professionals. Responsibility for receiving, collating, all paperwork in relation to all stock/non stock processing. The post holder will be required to travel to attend training and meetings, across South Warwickshire Foundation Trust. Communications and Working Relationships: To provide an effective administration service delivery in accordance with appropriate Trust policies and procedures and professional standards. To develop and maintain an effective communication network with service users, healthcare professionals and other statutory and voluntary organisations.
